title: EAGLE-3: Scaling up Inference Acceleration of Large Language Models via Training-Time Test
technique: Speculative decoding draft model that predicts tokens directly with multi-layer feature fusion and training-time test; drafting tree from EAGLE-2

optimized_metrics.evidence: Similarly, we aim to improve the acceptance rate and acceleration ratio of EAGLE by increasing its training data.
Similarly, we aim to improve the acceptance rate and acceleration ratio of EAGLE by increasing its training data.
EAGLE-3 does not modify the target model's weights and uses strict speculative sampling acceptance conditions, ensuring no loss in performance. Therefore, we do not evaluate generation quality.

headline_claim.text: EAGLE-3 achieves a speedup ratio up to 6.5x, with about 1.4x improvement over EAGLE-2. In the SGLang framework, EAGLE-3 achieves a 1.38x throughput improvement at a batch size of 64.

reported_metrics.where: Table 1, Fig 2 (speedup ratio vs vanilla autoregressive, batch size 1 HF-style runs)
Table 3 (SGLang, bs 2-64), Table 4 (bs=1 tokens/s on H100), Table 5 (vLLM, bs 2-56); headline only (re-pass)

metric_definitions.definition_quote: Speedup Ratio: The actual test speedup ratio relative to vanilla autoregressive decoding.
metric_definitions.notes: Wall-clock speedup of single-sequence decoding; not a latency distribution.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: Average Acceptance Length τ: The average number of tokens generated per drafting-verification cycle, which corresponds to the number of tokens accepted from the draft.
Acceptance Rate n-α: The proportion of draft tokens accepted, which directly reflects the draft model's approximation to the target model.
metric_definitions.notes: n = number of self-predicted inputs fed to the draft.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: Throughput at batch size = 1 on H100 ... 158.34 tokens/s (SGLang w/o speculative)
metric_definitions.notes: Throughput never formally defined; tokens/s in SGLang/vLLM benchmark tables, input/output token accounting unstated.

load_regime: Speedup: batch size 1 (greedy T=0 and T=1) on 5 tasks; throughput: fixed-batch-size sweep (SGLang bs 2-64 on H100, vLLM bs 2-56 on A100) on MT-Bench; no request-rate sweep
tradeoff_acknowledged: Speculative sampling gains shrink with batch size: in vLLM EAGLE shows max throughput gain at bs 24 and degrades throughput beyond; EAGLE-3 still +38% at bs 64 in SGLang (gain declines from batch 1 to 64).
hardware: Main speedup tables: not confirmed (RTX 3090 mentioned for a table); SGLang throughput on H100 (Table 3-4), vLLM throughput on A100 (Table 5)
extractor_notes: Lossless method: QUALITY recorded as constraint because paper says generation quality is not evaluated owing to strict acceptance. Speed is measured at batch size 1 for headline speedup (up to 6.5x), and the 1.38x throughput headline holds at bs 64 in SGLang; speedup at larger batch is much lower. Throughput tables were run by the SGLang team (as stated). Fixed batch, not load regime.
load_class_quote: Headline speedup at batch size 1 ("1.4x latency speedup over EAGLE-2 at batch size 1", §1) plus fixed-batch-size throughput sweeps ("1.38x throughput improvement at a batch size of 64", abstract); no request arrivals. = single-sequence + offline-batch
